issues.legal_issue: The market value of agricultural produce used in a business is determined by the ordinary-market-price method when the produce is ordinarily sold in the market, even if sales are regulated and there is no open market or more than one buyer.
material_facts: The company grew sugarcane and used it as raw material in its sugar-manufacturing business.
The company also bought sugarcane from registered and unregistered growers in ordinary commercial transactions, and its purchases exceeded its own production in some years.
The Sugarcane Control Order regulated sugarcane transactions and prices.

The company argued that sugarcane should be valued by cultivation costs and a reasonable profit because it was not ordinarily sold in a market; the court found that sugarcane was ordinarily sold and that the company’s own purchases demonstrated a market price.
issues.conclusion: The ordinary-market-price method applies to the sugarcane produced and used by the company. Where the price is controlled, the controlled price is the market price for this purpose.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 10(1) and 295(2)(b) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, and Rule 7(1) and Rule 7(2)(a)–(b) of the Income-tax Rules, 1962, the value of agricultural produce used in a business is determined by the average price when the produce is ordinarily sold in the market; the cultivation-cost method applies when it is not. A market does not require an open place where buyers and sellers congregate, or multiple buyers, and regulation does not make commercial sales cease to be market sales. The court distinguished J.M. Casey v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bihar & Orissa, where the purchases were not commercial, and relied on the market-valuation principles in Gift-Tax Officer, Calcutta v. Kastur Chand Jain, Ahmed G.H. Ariff v. Commissioner of Wealth-Tax, Building and Civil Engineering Holidays Scheme Management Ltd. v. Post Office, and the related hypothetical-market principle discussed in those authorities.

predicates.mixed_agricultural_business_income: The income being computed includes both agricultural activity and business activity, and agricultural produce is used in the business.
predicates.produce_ordinarily_sold: The agricultural produce is ordinarily sold in the relevant market or region.
predicates.commercial_purchases_occurred: The business regularly purchases the same produce from growers in ordinary commercial transactions.
predicates.apply_ordinary_market_price_method: The produce is valued using the ordinary market price, including a controlled price where applicable.

issues.definition: When mixed agricultural and business income is being computed, and the produce is ordinarily sold and bought in commercial transactions, the produce is valued using the ordinary market price.

issues.legal_issue: A court deciding a legal question in an income-tax reference does not direct a fresh investigation into facts that were not raised before the fact-finding tribunal when the findings already suffice to answer the question.
material_facts: The tribunal was the final fact-finding authority and had made findings on the facts underlying the legal questions referred to the High Court.
The assessee sought a direction for the tribunal to investigate factual matters that had not been raised before it.
The High Court had answered the referred questions on the existing findings and had no difficulty doing so.
issues.conclusion: The request for a fresh factual investigation was refused; the appeals and special leave petition concerning that request were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: In an income-tax reference, the High Court answers the referred legal questions on the facts found by the tribunal and cannot go behind those findings. Fresh investigation into facts not raised before the tribunal is not permissible at the reference stage. A supplementary statement may be called for if incomplete factual findings prevent the court from answering a referred question, but that circumstance was absent here.

predicates.income_tax_reference_case: A court is considering a legal question referred in an income-tax matter on the basis of findings made by the fact-finding tribunal.
predicates.new_fact_questions_not_raised_before_tri: A party asks for investigation of factual questions that it did not raise before the tribunal.
predicates.existing_findings_suffice: The facts found by the tribunal are sufficient for the court to answer the referred legal question.
predicates.deny_fresh_fact_investigation: The court refuses a request for fresh investigation into facts at the reference stage.

issues.definition: In an income-tax reference, if a party seeks investigation of factual questions it did not raise before the tribunal and the existing findings suffice, the court refuses fresh factual investigation.
